notes:
CIRCUIT: five inverting op-amp stages, same family as circuit_891. Every triangle is drawn with '-' on the upper-left lead, '+' on the lower-left lead and the output at the right apex, and every one carries its feedback element from the '-' input back to the output. Four of the five have their '+' input strapped to GND; A2 (#3, top right) instead has its '+' input driven from the big centre node. Sources: 5V V-DC (#6) top-left, 10A I-DC (#20) bottom-left. 24 components, 12 nets.

NET MAP
  0   = ground: GND #7 #9 #14 #21 #22 #23, V-DC #6 bottom lead, I-DC #20 bottom lead, and the '+' inputs of A1(#4), A4(#10), A3(#15), A5(#18).
  n3  = V-DC #6 top lead + left plate of C1(#1, 1uF) + '-' input of A1(#4); the y~182 rail from x=125 to x=259, T at (223,184).
  n4  = right plate of C1(#1) + output of A1(#4) + left end of R1(#5, 1k); the y~210 wire from the apex to x=454 (T there) and on to the resistor.
  n1  = right end of R1(#5) + left end of L1(#0, 1uH) + '-' input of A2(#3); the y~208 wire, T at (584,208).
  n2  = right end of L1(#0) + output of A2(#3) + left end of R2(#2, 1k); the y~220 wire, T at (828,220).
  n5  = the right-hand rail x~970..984 running from y~222 down to y~763: right end of R2(#2), right end of R4(#11) (T at (984,504)), right end of R5(#17). Three terminals and nothing else, exactly as drawn.
  n6  = the centre node at the solder dot (515,473): '+' input of A2(#3) via the staircase up to (600,240), right end of L2(#13), output of A3(#15) via the x~380 stub (dot at (380,486)), left end of R3(#12), and the right plate of C3(#19) via the x~517 column down to y~756.
  n9  = I-DC #20 top lead + left end of L2(#13) + '-' input of A3(#15); the y~640 wire, T at (220,636).
  n7  = right end of R3(#12) + left plate of C2(#8, 1uF) + '-' input of A4(#10); the y~468 wire plus the x~638 column up to y~402 (see MERGE below).
  n8  = right plate of C2(#8) + output of A4(#10) + left end of R4(#11); the y~494 wire, T at (785,494).
  n10 = left plate of C3(#19) + left end of L3(#16, 1uH) + '-' input of A5(#18); the y~756 wire, T at (628,754).
  n11 = right end of L3(#16) + output of A5(#18) + left end of R5(#17); the y~761 wire plus the x~783 column up to y~685 (see MERGE below).

SITE DECISIONS (every CRITICAL site explicitly ruled; none needed overriding - this sheet contains no wire crossings at all, only Ts, and the drafter put a visible solder blob on most of them):
  S12 (223,184) junction - T with a small dot: the C1 feedback column drops onto the V-DC/A1-input rail. Crossing would strand C1's left plate and remove A1's feedback.
  S13 (584,208) junction - T with a dot: L1's left column drops onto the R1->A2 input wire.
  S14 (454,210) junction - T: C1's right-plate column ends on the A1 output wire.
  S15 (828,220) junction - T: L1's right column ends on the A2 output wire.
  S36 (515,473) junction - 4-way with an unmistakable round solder blob (dot score 3.0, the largest on the sheet). The tracer also reported hop=5.7, which is spurious - the 4x crop shows a filled dot with four straight branches, no arc and no jog. Crossing would split the L2/A3-output rail from the x~517 column and separate A2's '+' input from R3 and C3, giving 14 nets instead of 12.
  S39 (380,486) junction - T with a large dot: A3's output stub rises from y=650 and lands on the L2/centre rail. Only three branches, so crossing is not even geometrically available.
  S40 (785,494) junction - T: C2's right-plate column ends on the A4 output wire (verified in edges.py: e54 from (744,404) to (785,491) meets e84/e85, the apex-to-R4 run).
  S46 (984,504) junction - T with a dot: R4's right lead ends on the right-hand vertical rail. Crossing would leave R4's right terminal on a one-terminal net.
  S51 (220,636) junction - T: L2's left column drops onto the I-DC/A3-input wire.
  S63 (628,754) junction - T with a dot: L3's left column drops onto the C3/A5-input wire.
  Non-critical sites S3-S8, S11, S16, S17, S19, S21, S22, S24, S28-S33, S35, S45, S47, S49, S52-S54, S57, S58, S60, S61, S64-S67 are all handwriting ('1uF', '1uH', '1kOhm', '5V', '10A') or symbol ink brushing a wire, or corners inside a net that is already correct; defaults left alone.

PORT / PIN FIXES
  Terminals that had landed on handwriting (each produced a one-terminal net):
    #1 Capacitor t1: was p2@(359,151), a stroke of '1uF'. Moved to p1@(398,122), the real right plate lead.
    #6 V-DC t1: was p2@(163,216), a stroke of '5V'. Moved to p1@(122,270), the real bottom lead running to GND #9.
    #16 Inductor t1: was p1@(753,647), a stroke of '1uH'. Moved to p4@(759,685), the real right lead (wire length 58).
    #20 I-DC t0: was p1@(54,696), a stroke of the '0' in '10A'. Moved to p2@(103,755), the real bottom lead to GND #22.
    #8 Capacitor t0: was p2@(699,371), stray ink above the box. Moved to p1@(692,401), the real left plate lead (wire length 51).
  Op-amp pin order (required in+, in-, out). All five triangles read '-' upper-left, '+' lower-left, output at the apex; the tracer's default order was wrong on every one:
    #4  -> t0=p3(258,229)='+', t1=p1(259,185)='-', t2=p0(357,210)=out   (p2@(357,168) was stray '1uF' ink)
    #3  -> t0=p0(628,248)='+', t1=p2(629,205)='-', t2=p1(744,222)=out
    #10 -> t0=p0(635,522)='+', t1=p3(635,463)='-', t2=p2(757,494)=out   (p1@(638,435) is the same column as p3 but on the far side of the box cut - see MERGE)
    #15 -> t0=p2(241,680)='+', t1=p1(240,635)='-', t2=p0(370,646)=out
    #18 -> t0=p2(668,801)='+', t1=p0(667,753)='-', t2=p3(786,761)=out   (the tracer had t0 on p1@(783,719), which is the L3 feedback column brushing the box corner, not the output lead)
  Each is corroborated by the resulting negative-feedback path: C1 on A1, L1 on A2, L2 on A3, C2 on A4, L3 on A5.

MERGE (two nets were split purely by the component-box subtraction, not by any real gap in the ink)
  ["8.0","12.1"]: the C2 left-plate column runs down x~638 from y=402 to the y~468 wire that carries R3's right lead into A4's '-' input. The tracer's skeleton stops at (638,435) and restarts at (631,467) because A4's annotated box (x 638..754, y 440..574) swallows the segment in between. inkmap at (638,452) shows unbroken 3 px ink from y=430 straight down to the T at y=467-469, and the S35 crop shows the column and the horizontal meeting cleanly. Merging puts C2's left plate, R3's right lead and A4's '-' input on one net (n7), as drawn.
  ["16.1","17.0"]: L3's right-hand column runs down x~783 from y=685 past A5's apex to the y~761 output wire that feeds R5. A5's box (x 670..783, y 723..843) cuts it, leaving edge e116 (783,719)->(759,685) and edge e126 (808,761)->(786,761) unconnected. inkmap at (786,740) shows unbroken ink at x=782-785 from y=716 down through y=764, and inkmap at (775,765) shows the triangle apex, the column and the R5 wire all meeting at (770-785, 761). Merging puts L3's right lead, A5's output and R5's left lead on one net (n11), as drawn.

CLASSES: no reclassification needed. Every symbol matches its label (two plates = Capacitor 1uF, coils = Inductor 1uH, zigzag = Resistor 1k, circle with +/- = V-DC 5V, circle with an up arrow = I-DC 10A, triangle = Op-Amp, hatch = GND).

UNRESOLVED: none. The only oddity is n5, a three-terminal node holding the far ends of the three output resistors with no further load - identical to the corresponding node in circuit_891 and unambiguous in the ink (the right-hand rail runs continuously from (970,222) down to (970,763) with T-joins at each resistor).
